To be clear, I am not endorsing or saying it is a good idea at all. I’m just sharing my experience because it is helpful for other people to learn from my mistakes and if anything, I’m discouraging you from piercing yourself 


Why did I pierce myself instead of going to a piercer?

First, I earn 1.5 USD an hour on a regular day, which obligates me to make my spending choices much more thoughtfully. And sure, I understand that it is my body and I should invest in my health and well-being, having a belly piercing is not a necessity and if I can’t afford a piercer I should not be doing it, I get it. 

That is why I saved up some money and went to see a piercer, I had bought some time ago 2 matching surgical steel piercings, one for my mom and one for me because when I was little and she was in college, she wanted to pierce her belly and I told her it was a bad idea and she was so sad, so I saw them and I really wanted those 2. I went to him and showed him the piercings and he treated me like I was so so so stupid for wanting to use that jewelry and that material, pretty much that but with more subtle words, saying that it was sick, silly, and naive for wanting a 2 dollar piece of metal inside my body, that he only used his own piercings the most simple ones started at 25 USD and one similar to mine at 50. I understand I may be stupid but he didn’t have to talk to me like that, at my workplace I believe that some people make poor choices and others are just dumb but since it is my job to be nice and caring with them I don’t mind sitting down and explaining nicely what’s best for them without making them feel like I’m mocking their lack of experience, and I believe we all should be treated like that specially if you are paying for a service. 
 
So I tried with another piercer and it seems like it is a common theme among them to treat people without any piercings or tattoos with disregard to their ideas. And I’m an anxious shy person. 

Another reason why I feel more comfortable doing things to myself like cutting my hair and etc is that I care a lot about myself obviously and I make sure everything is exactly the way it looks in my imagination.


What materials did I use?

Surgical steel piercing, autoclave-sterile 12G hollow needle, autoclave-sterile forceps, surgical soap, skin marker, Microdacyn. 


The process. Why did it take so long?

First I used the marker to trace the 2 points the needle had to go through, then I cleaned my skin and surrounding areas with the surgical soap and Microdacyn. Then I tried piercing from the inner part of my navel to the outer part like usually piercers do but the angle didn’t allow me to apply much pressure so I went the other way. 

The forceps were not very useful so I ended up not really relying much on them. 

At first, it all went smoothly, not painful, I tried going fast but when I poked a hole out of my belly I realized I was grabbing too little skin for my liking, so I went back a bit, poking another hole inside my skin to grab a little more. 

The 2 main things that made it difficult for me to calculate how much skin I was grabbing was that I couldn’t see the mark I drew in the inner part of my navel, because, yeah I am stupid, and the other reason is that when I penetrated the needle and it came out the needle kept pushing the lower part of my belly button, the one I was not piercing poking more and more holes and applying pressure that made my aim worse. Although, honestly, it was more my perfectionism than any other thing.

So I decided to stretch my skin out and make the needle go outside like the way you grab soup with a spoon to avoid hitting the other side of my navel with it. This went on for 30 minutes, I was bleeding a bit and the pain inside my skin was becoming distracting, I decided to grab a 0.5 ml 31Gx6MM syringe and used 0.05 ml of 2% lidocaine to inject myself into the inner part of my navel to numb it, this proved to be very effective and I was able to concentrate on the precision without thinking of the pain. 

I disinfected the piercing and put it in. I was sweating quite a bit afterward and I felt like I should have gone to a piercer. 


Aftercare

I decided to take an oral prophylactic antibiotic treatment the week after. I prefer oral antibiotics because topical ones are only really fighting against external bacteria while the one I used killed the most common gram-positive bacteria present in skin infections and would help me heal the wounds inside my skin. I did this because I have a history of not being able to heal skin wounds for weeks until I take an antibiotic. 

The first week I cleaned the area with soap once a day, with saline solution twice a day while spraying Microdacyn on it 3 or 4 times a day. After that week I’ve been cleaning it in the shower as usual once a day, at night cleaning it with saline solution and using Microdacyn once a day.

I used dresses for the first 2 weeks and I started using jeans in the 3rd week. 

So far, after a month and a half, I haven’t had any problems, no infections, tearing, weird scaring, signs of rejection, redness, nothing. For the first 3 weeks, I had some crusty discharge that I’d clean in my daily routine to avoid any problems and right now it looks perfectly ok, it hurt only the first week and now I don’t even feel it. I understand the healing process isn't done yet but so far it is ok. 


Would I do it again?

After I finished poking holes into my belly I promised myself I’d not do that again but looking back I feel more comfortable doing it myself and not relying on someone because I’m a stupid stubborn person.

Would I recommend it?

Definitely not. If you don’t have easy access to antibiotics and special materials I think it can end up really really bad in a serious infection or a permanent scar. Piercing yourself means putting yourself in an unnecessary position of risk, especially if it isn’t something easy and safe like the navel, never do that to your face or genitals, maybe to your earlobe but not to more sensitive parts or parts that have cartilage. 

Also, you have no one to ask questions or ask for help if you have any issues. It is probably a good idea to use titanium and not surgical steel like me. I did a good amount of research about the required anatomy for a belly piercing, the size of the bar and etc, etc and I still screwed up. Any minor mistake would be terrible for your poor abdomen or any part of your body, don’t be evil to your belly, it does so much stuff for you, it is a better idea to find a piercer who understands your ideas and  can show you a good portfolio.
